thread:
oliver: heads up — following the autoscaler RFC, I prototyped a hybrid approach: lightweight local delegates per-pool + a central coordinator for global policy. wanted quick sync on failure/fallback patterns.
kim: curious — what's the delegate responsibility boundary vs central?
omiver: delegate handles immediate admission, short-lived probe warmups, and local headroom bookkeeping. central coordinator enforces cross-pool fairness, reconciles long-term reservations, and issues global evictions.
maya: does delegate keep state that survives restarts? that's a big ops concern.
oliver: minimal durable state — delegates keep in-memory sliding counters + a small raft-backed checkpoint for outstanding reservations. on restart they fetch leases from central to rehydrate.
raj: how do we avoid split-brain when coordinator is partitioned? we saw bad behavior in the last canary where two controllers raced and double-admitted.
oliver: good point. design idea: delegates accept only token-bearing admissions. central mints time-limited tokens (10s default). if coordinator unreachable, delegates can operate in degraded mode using cached tokens and a local conservative fallback window.
kim: Token minting feels like building a new distributed lock. any simpler option?
oliver: alternative: optimistic local admission with periodic reconciler that issues compensating evictions. downside: user-visible request failures when reconciler corrects.
maya: tradeoff analysis pls — user latency vs correctness.
oliver: short: tokens = slightly more latency on admission path (1 API call to coordinator cached), but much less chance of rolling back requests. optimistic = lower admission latency but higher tail risk.
raj: what about noisy neighbors on preemptible nodes? we need a spillover strategy for bursts.
oliver: plan: burst credits per-tenant + a shared ephemeral spillover pool. delegates first consume tenant credits, then try cross-tenant spillover via coordinator. if both exhausted, admission denied with hint to client to retry to a lower-slo model.
kim: can we return structured error to SDK so it can downgrade automatically?
maya: yes, we should use a structured JSON error shape: {"code":"POOL_EXHAUSTED","suggested_action":"downgrade:model-small, retry_after:1500"} — SDK can map to fallback.
raj: how do we measure when to prewarm vs rely on spillover? need heuristics.
oliver: we want a probe-based prewarm: if request queue shows growth rate > alpha for window T, delegates allocate prewarm slots up to X. heuristics: alpha = 20% increase per 5s, T=15s. can be tuned per-tenant.
kim: include a cheap probe: send a tiny zero-shot request to tenant's pinned model to create KV cache. cost is N tokens but 90% fewer than full prewarm.
oliver: exactly. we call it "probe-warmup". sample snippet for delegate config: 

```
delegate:
  probe_window: 15s
  probe_alpha: 0.2
  probe_budget_per_min: 10
  token_ttl_secs: 10
  local_headroom_percent: 12
```

raj: what about eviction signals? users hit errors during reconciler-driven evictions last month. need graceful draining.
maya: graceful steps: 1) stop admitting new burst requests 2) mark node/pool as draining 3) wait for inflight tokens to finish (TTL) 4) if still overcommit, soft-evict oldest low-priority sessions with a 5s pre-notify.
oliver: proposed eviction API shape for delegates: `POST /v1/evict` with payload {"pool":"p1","mode":"soft|force","targets":[ids],"deadline_ms":5000}. delegates should try soft first.
kim: ops wants an emergency override path to force-drain a pool when hardware is failing. include `force` with audit log requirement.
oliver: yes — force operations require two authorized approvals and emit an ops event: `ops-bot: EMERGENCY_DRAIN pool=p1 approvers=[kim,raj]`.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: autoscaler/delegate v0.3.4 -> canary to pool-alpha at 14:00 UTC.
raj: sanity check — metrics we need exposed ASAP: per-tenant credits_used, local_headroom_free, probe_success_rate, token_mint_latency, reconcile_conflicts_count, evictions_soft_count, evictions_force_count.
maya: add metric `admission_downgrade_count` so we know how often SDK had to fallback.
kim: logging: include admission trace id so we can correlate SDK fallback with pool events.
oliver: good. on the orchestration side, we must define operator rollback: automatic rollback if canary increases reconcile_conflicts_count > 5/min or probe_failure_rate > 20% for 10m.
raj: do we need an escape hatch where delegates temporarily stop issuing tokens and flip to central-only admission?
oliver: yes — central-only mode for delegates when they detect coordinator partition > 30s. delegate config: `fallback_mode: central_only | local_cautious | optimistic`. default `local_cautious`.
maya: who owns the rollout doc? I can draft the failure-mode playbook.
oliver: perfect. O: can you own the canary and rollout checklist?
maya: yes, I'll draft. checklist items: metrics probe, rollback triggers, ops override steps, SDK error contract, canary tenant list.
kim: one more: storage cost — raft-backed checkpoints might be heavy at scale. maybe we just keep leases in central (single source) and delegates rehydrate via central snapshot on start.
oliver: agreed, simplified: central persists leases, delegates fetch on start and keep ephemeral cache; checkpoint removed. reduces complexity.
raj: wrap-up decision proposals?
oliver: summary: 1) implement delegates with ephemeral state + token-based admissions 2) central coordinator persists leases + mints time-limited tokens 3) probe-warmup to reduce full prewarm cost 4) burst credits + shared spillover pool 5) soft-first eviction API + force with 2-approver audit 6) rollout gates + automatic rollback on defined metrics.
maya: LGTM, will draft the playbook and SDK contract.
kim: I'll add metric dashboards and an alert for reconcile_conflicts_count.
raj: schedule a 30m follow-up tomorrow to review the canary checklist.
oliver: added — ping me if edge-cases crop up. :thumbsup:
